text:
rachel: Heads-up: prototype for an alternate cold-start path where origin serves a single compressed safetensors shard and our edge+client run an incremental extractor. Target: mobile SDKs and flaky CDNs. Thoughts?

tom: sounds useful. main question: do we require the extractor to run client-side (mobile) or on-edge (edge node) before populating GPU pages? Mobile CPU budget is tiny.

rachel: POC ran extractor on edge node (sidecar) and wrote pages into our shared on-disk cache. Client just streamed bytes and waited for first pages to become available. Mobile only needs to download, validate signature, and spin.

priya: ok. Two concerns: 1) ensuring the extracted page offsets match the page layout used by the runtime, and 2) safety when a new model rollout replaces the shard while extraction is in-flight.

leo: for (1) we should bake a canonical page map into the blob header. Minimal header JSON (fixed-size first block) describing tensors with offsets, shapes, dtype and checksum. That way the extractor can write pages into the correct file offsets.

jordan: for (2) add a UUID for the shard + signed manifest that includes model_version. Extractor verifies manifest signature (ed25519) and refuses to ingest if the runtime has switched to a different model_version. We can also use ETag semantics from origin.

rachel: implementation sketch: compressed shard is served at /model/<id>/shard-0.gzblob. The first 2048 bytes are an ASCII JSON header then gzip stream. Edge accepts Range/HEAD but fallback to /gzblob when range unsupported.

priya: how does resumability work? If the extractor dies mid-extract, we must be able to resume without re-downloading entire blob.

leo: make extractor write a small per-page state file with statuses: pending, writing, done. On restart it reads existing page flags and seeks into the gz stream to the next needed tensor. For seeking in gz, we can produce an index of gzip-block offsets at shard-creation time and embed that in header. That keeps device CPU low and allows efficient resume.

jordan: minor addition: expose an X-Extract-Job header and correlating metric tag so we can see how many extracts per shard and retries.

rachel: what about atomicity in the cache namespace? If extractor writes pages directly to in-use page files we must avoid readers seeing partial pages. Use a write-then-rename strategy: write to tmp page file, fsync, then atomic rename to final path or flip a per-page bit in metadata atomically.

priya: rename/finalize is good. Also use a per-shard lock/token so eviction won't remove partially-populated shards. Eviction should respect extract-in-progress tokens.

leo: eviction TTL idea: extractors set a short pin (30s) on pages they just wrote; after finalize we convert pin into normal LRU ranking. Configs: extract.pin_ttl, extract.parallelism, extract-max-retries. Defaults: 30s, 4, 3.

rachel: security: header manifest must be signed. Clients/edge verify signature using model's public key bundle. We should reject unsigned blobs. Also log signature failures to SLO dashboards.

jordan: ops: store gz blobs only in regions where fallback is enabled. Otherwise we waste storage. Provide lifecycle: gc gzblobs after N days unless flagged.

priya: performance tradeoffs: network wins (fewer small range RTTs) vs CPU cost for extraction and more egress if we double-store. We need to quantify cost per-GB and impact on TTFB for 3G/4G. The POC numbers looked promising for >100MB shards.

tom: SDK integration notes: mobile should try index-first via range. Only if range fails/slow beyond threshold do we hit gzblob. Also provide a low-CPU path where mobile streams but delegates extraction to edge via X-Delegate-Extract header.

leo: telemetry: emit extract_attempts, extract_success, extract_resume_count, extract_cpu_secs, signed_manifest_failures, pinned_evictions. Add SLO alert if extract_success_rate < 99% in any region.

rachel: rollout plan: feature flag per model + region. Phase 1: edge-only extraction (no mobile CPU), flag off globally. Phase 2: widen to mobile delegate extraction, test in APAC. Phase 3: allow client-side extract if mobile device meets CPU/memory predicate.

jordan: engineering tasks: shard creator produces gzip-indexed blobs + manifest signer; origin nginx serves gzblob; edge-sidecar extractor; page finalize API; SDK detection logic.

priya: +1. One more safety idea: if extractor detects mismatched layout_version between blob and runtime, it should abort and emit a distinct error to prevent silent corruption.

rachel: great. I'll write a short RFC capturing header schema, signature scheme, resume index, extractor semantics (tmp-write + atomic finalize), eviction pin semantics, config knobs and metrics. Will ping @tom @priya for review.

devops-bot: Created feature flags: fallback_gzblob (off), extract_edge_worker (off). Use /ops/flags to enable per-region.
